name: MomentumForge — Adaptive Study Progress Tracker
description: A self-built productivity system that tracks daily, weekly, and monthly study goals with real-time progress, XP-based gamification, and automatic rescheduling for missed tasks.
live: FILL IN — your deployed live link
github: FILL IN — your GitHub repo link
problem: Study plans often break down the moment a task is missed — progress becomes hard to track across daily, weekly, and monthly goals, and missed work quietly falls through the cracks. MomentumForge keeps every view in sync in real time and automatically resurfaces missed tasks instead of letting them disappear.
features: Interconnected Daily, Weekly, and Monthly views — completing one task instantly updates all three
One-click task completion with XP rewards and streak tracking
Live dashboard showing today's, weekly, monthly, and overall completion percentages, calculated in real time
Auto-rescheduling — missed tasks roll forward automatically and are flagged with the exact number of days overdue
Custom-built bar and donut charts on the stats page, written from scratch in vanilla JS with no charting libraries
Difficulty alerts that auto-flag heavier topics (e.g. Recursion, Graphs, DP, Trees) and allocate extra prep time
Command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K) for instant search across the entire roadmap
Branded print/PDF export that generates a clean, letterhead-style document instead of a raw screen printout
Light/Dark mode with an animated toggle
Firebase Authentication — email/password and Google sign-in, with a 'Remember me' option
Local data persistence with JSON backup/restore
Fully responsive across mobile, tablet, and desktop
decisions: Chose vanilla JavaScript over a framework to keep full control over performance and to hand-build the charting and command-palette logic myself rather than relying on libraries. Added Firebase Authentication specifically for secure login/signup, including Google sign-in, without having to stand up a full custom backend just for identity.
challenges: Building the bar and donut charts from scratch in vanilla JS — including responsive scaling and real-time updates as tasks are completed — without any charting library. Also designing the auto-rescheduling logic so a missed task rolls forward correctly and reports an accurate overdue count without duplicating or losing data.
tradeoffs: Data lives in the browser's localStorage rather than a cloud database, so progress doesn't automatically sync across devices — JSON backup/restore is the current workaround. Firebase is used only for authentication, which keeps the app lightweight, but it means logging in on a new device doesn't yet bring your saved data with it.
